papers.title: Irreversible functional network deformation induced by preprocessing scheme order in multivariate EEG recordings.
papers.summary: The paper quantitatively compares two EEG preprocessing schemes that differ only in the order of filtering and re-referencing, using sleep EEG, synthetic models, and surrogate testing. It shows that re-referencing followed by filtering induces spurious cross-correlations that increase with frequency band and spectral exponent, becoming irreversible for steep spectra (β ≥ 2), whereas filtering followed by re-referencing introduces only small, correctable negative shifts; the authors recommend filtering followed by re-referencing with surrogate correction for such signals.

papers.title: Window leakage in clinical EEG machine learning: matched subject-independent evaluation across ADHD and Parkinson cohorts.
papers.summary: The paper defines 'window leakage' in EEG machine learning, where segments from the same participant appear in both training and testing sets, and evaluates its impact across ADHD and Parkinson's cohorts. Using participant-disjoint evaluation, balanced accuracy dropped from 95.59% to 60.98% in ADHD and from 92.02% to 56.17% in Parkinson's, demonstrating that random-window splits inflate performance estimates and that valid generalization requires subject-level separation.

papers.title: NESTApp: A GUI-Based MATLAB Application for Auditable TMS-EEG Preprocessing with EEGLAB
papers.summary: The paper describes NESTApp, a GUI-based MATLAB application built on EEGLAB for constructing, applying, and automatically documenting customizable TMS-EEG preprocessing pipelines with integrated quality control. Applied to 29 recordings from 16 participants, NESTApp processed 27 and identified those requiring further inspection, aiming to improve reproducibility and lower technical barriers in TMS-EEG preprocessing.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Fatigue Detection from EEG Signals: A Methodological Pilot Framework with Potential for Nursing Applications.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical practice and research
papers.summary: This pilot study used EEG features with machine learning to predict fatigue and found that Random Forest achieved perfect 5-fold cross-validation performance (accuracy=1.00), but performance dropped under subject-independent LOSO validation (accuracy=0.97, macro-F1=0.91), highlighting the need for realistic validation in fatigue detection.

papers.title: Visual cues in MI-BCI induce biases in EEG classification models with deep learning but not with standard machine learning.
papers.summary: This study evaluated whether including visual cue onset in EEG windows biases deep learning models for motor imagery BCI classification. It found that visual cue onset significantly improved accuracy for DeepConvNet and REVE, but attribution maps showed these models relied on cue-related visual evoked potentials rather than motor imagery sensorimotor rhythms (ERD/ERS), while CSP+LDA maintained consistent motor cortex activation and minimal accuracy change.

papers.title: Clinical validation of autoSCORE: A human-in-the-loop AI tool for interpretation of long-term EEG recordings.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: The study clinically validated autoSCORE, a convolutional neural network integrated into an EEG reader, for analyzing long-term EEG recordings within a human-in-the-loop workflow. Across 80 2-hour segments, autoSCORE's accuracy was comparable to human experts, and in the human-in-the-loop workflow, inspecting the top 10 automated markers per category enabled correct identification of all abnormal segments by reviewing only 1.5-5.5% of the recording.

papers.title: An Explainable Self-Supervised Temporal Transformer for Participant-Level Classification of Depressive Symptoms From Resting-State EEG.
papers.journal: International journal of methods in psychiatric research
papers.summary: The paper develops an explainable self-supervised temporal transformer for participant-level classification of BDI-defined elevated depressive symptoms from resting-state EEG, using masked temporal pretraining and supervised fine-tuning. The model achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.82 (95% CI 0.73–0.90) and balanced accuracy of 0.75, with self-supervised pretraining improving performance over no pretraining (ROC-AUC 0.74), while explainability analyses identified temporally relevant intervals and frontal-midline to centro-parietal channel contributions; the authors caution that findings do not establish clinical diagnostic validity.

papers.title: Robust Functional Ward's Linkages With Applications in EEG Data Clustering.
papers.summary: The paper proposes two robust functional Ward-type linkages for hierarchical clustering of grouped functional data, using magnitude-shape outlyingness and modified band depth to select central curves, and demonstrates their robustness and competitive performance in simulations and EEG data analyses.

papers.title: Selective Auditory Attention Decoding with a Two-Node Wireless EEG Sensor Network
papers.summary: Evaluated selective auditory attention decoding using a two-node wireless around-ear EEG sensor network and achieved 69.24% accuracy on 60s windows, improving to 77.17% steady-state with HMM post-processing and 32.79s attention switch detection time.

papers.title: Human-artificial intelligence collaboration for comanaging epilepsy in real time.
papers.summary: This paper presents a device platform that uses a large language model-based AI to converse bidirectionally with patients through a smartphone app, processing EEG biomarkers to help manage epilepsy in real time. In a validation with 13 patients, the platform provided seizure notifications and recorded patient feedback, which improved seizure detector precision in a pseudoprospective simulation without expert intervention.

papers.title: An EEG-based framework for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis via single-channel multi-entropy fusion and ensemble learning.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers. Part H, Journal of engineering in medicine
papers.summary: Developed a single-channel EEG framework combining wavelet and empirical mode decomposition with multi-entropy features and ensemble learning, achieving 97.92% and 81.54% accuracy on two public datasets for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis.

papers.title: Robust Detection of Major Depressive Disorder Using Empirical Mode Decomposition-Based EEG Signal Analysis.
papers.summary: The paper develops a major depressive disorder (MDD) detection system using EEG signals processed with empirical mode decomposition (EMD) to extract instantaneous amplitude and frequency features from intrinsic mode functions. Using SVM with a linear kernel and PCA dimensionality reduction, the system achieved perfect classification (100% accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, and negative predictive value) in a public dataset of 16 MDD and 16 healthy subjects.

papers.title: Decoding object categories from electroencephalography during free viewing reveals early information evolution compared to passive viewing.
papers.summary: This study combined multivariate pattern analysis with deconvolution to decode object category information from EEG during free viewing and compared it to passive viewing. It found that category information could be decoded from individual fixations in free viewing, generalized across conditions, and emerged earlier when time-locked to fixation onset than to stimulus onset, suggesting parafoveal processing.

papers.title: Gamma transcranial alternating current stimulation prevents scopolamine-induced damage to EEG activity and spatial memory.
papers.summary: Pre-administered 40 Hz transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) targeting the hippocampus prevented scopolamine-induced reductions in spontaneous and task-related gamma EEG activity and spatial memory deficits in mice, with dual-site tACS reversing memory impairment.

papers.title: Does chronic occupational demand alter EEG stress biomarkers during cognitive challenge? a study of emergency physicians.
papers.summary: In 17 emergency physicians and 18 controls, acute cognitive challenge robustly increased frontocentral theta and suppressed alpha, but no significant group differences emerged after correction, suggesting chronic occupational demand does not alter these EEG stress biomarkers for large effects.

papers.title: VAD-EmotionNet: a spatial-spectral attention network for EEG emotion recognition in the 3D affective space.
papers.summary: VAD-EmotionNet, a spatial-spectral attention network with Hilbert-Huang transform features and cosine temporal inference correction, achieved competitive performance on DEAP and DREAMER for EEG emotion recognition in 3D valence-arousal-dominance space.

papers.title: Characterization of the Bispectral Index in Healthy Volunteers Receiving Inhalation Anesthetics in Combination With Opioids in a Randomized Trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized trial with 211 healthy volunteers, BIS50 and BIS95 values were estimated for five anesthetic regimens; the BIS index strongly predicted responsiveness (AUC ≥0.95), and adding opioids to sevoflurane had minimal impact on these thresholds.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Microstate Dynamics and their Associations with Acclimatization Index and Serum Albumin in Healthy Adults with Chronic High-Altitude Exposure.
papers.summary: This study compared resting-state EEG microstate dynamics between low-altitude and high-altitude healthy adults; high-altitude exposure was associated with increased Microstate A duration and GEV, decreased occurrence, and altered transitions, with serum albumin mediating some associations with acclimatization index.

papers.title: Dynamic EEG network responses to acupuncture stimulation in patients with stroke: a neurophysiological study.
papers.summary: Acupuncture at Jianyu, Quchi, and Waiguan in stroke patients produced frequency-dependent short-term changes in EEG power (delta, theta, alpha) and whole-brain functional connectivity (delta wPLI decrease, alpha increase), without significant network topology changes.

papers.title: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) in schizophrenia: enhancing transparency in clinical decision-making.
papers.summary: This review discusses how explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) can improve transparency and clinical trust in machine learning models for schizophrenia, which often use multimodal neuroimaging and clinical data to predict diagnosis, treatment response, and relapse risk. It argues that XAI-integrated models can support biomarker discovery and personalized psychiatry while maintaining ethical and regulatory standards.

papers.title: Default mode network mechanisms of trait rumination in treatment-resistant depression and rTMS: evidence from source-localized EEG.
papers.summary: In 66 treatment-resistant depression patients undergoing rTMS, baseline rumination severity was specifically associated with higher alpha-band amplitude envelope correlation within the default mode network, a stable trait-like marker unaffected by 30 rTMS sessions.

papers.title: Changes in clinical management related to continuous versus routine EEG in critically ill adults: analysis of a randomized trial.
papers.summary: This ancillary analysis of the CERTA randomized trial compared continuous EEG versus repeated routine EEG in 364 critically ill adults and found that clinical management changes, especially anti-seizure medication adjustments, were more frequent with continuous EEG (58.2% vs 45.6%, p=0.018; ASM 22.0% vs 12.1%, p=0.012), but mortality and functional outcomes at 6 months remained similar.

papers.title: Optimized hybrid Transformer-based model for EEG classification: application to wheelchair control.
papers.summary: This study systematically compared simple and hybrid deep learning architectures for EEG-based motor imagery classification and found that a Transformer + CNN hybrid achieved perfect classification accuracy (1.00), flawless AUC (1.000), zero misclassifications, and competitive inference time (1.17 s), supporting its use in real-time brain-computer interface wheelchair control.

papers.title: Chronic Electrophysiology Captures Progressive Variability in DNA-Damaged Cardiac Networks
papers.summary: Using a microelectrode array system, this study chronically recorded electrophysiological activity from human iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte monolayers for up to 40 days, capturing progressive declines in field potential amplitude, conduction velocity, and increased beat-to-beat variability after doxorubicin exposure. Electrode-resolved analyses revealed spatial variability in cardiotoxic responses that would be masked by population averages, and endpoint assays confirmed reduced calcium transients, mitochondrial membrane potential, and connexin 43 loss.

papers.title: Short-term subjective and EEG responses following cervical rotatory manipulation are not reproduced by simulated cracking sound: A randomized controlled study.
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial with 54 healthy volunteers, cervical rotatory manipulation (CRM) improved positive affect, comfort, and satisfaction and altered frontal alpha/beta ratio and alpha band connectivity compared to sham manipulations, while simulated cracking sound did not reproduce these effects.

papers.title: Multimodal Evidence for Large-scale Network Imbalance in Etomidate Use Disorder.
papers.summary: Simultaneous EEG-fNIRS in 54 individuals with etomidate use disorder and 46 healthy controls found delta-band network decoupling and reduced frontal hemodynamic connectivity, with weaker primary motor cortex–inferior frontal gyrus connectivity associated with stronger negative reinforcement craving (rho=-0.471). An exploratory random forest model achieved the highest test-set AUC (0.80) for discriminating the groups.

papers.title: Relief Emerges as an Offset-Locked Emotional Response: Self-Reported and Neural Evidence.
papers.summary: Using an offset-locked paradigm with continuous self-reports and EEG in 30 healthy adults, this study found that aversive auditory stimulus offsets elicited the steepest self-reported affective change and a clear N1-P2 complex with larger P2 amplitude than sustained stimulation, indicating that relief is a discrete offset-locked emotional event rather than a passive return to baseline.

papers.title: Associations Between Resting-State EEG Delta-band Activity at Selected Parietal Electrodes and Cognitive Changes Following Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation in Patients with Mild Cognitive Impairment: An Exploratory Analysis.
papers.summary: Exploratory secondary analysis of 26 MCI patients from a randomized sham-controlled taVNS trial found that parietal delta-band power changes correlated with cognitive changes after 24 weeks, with taVNS-related MoCA-B improvement positively associated with relative delta-power changes at P1, P2, and P5 (r=0.629–0.652). Correlations did not survive multiple-comparison correction but were consistent across electrodes, supporting parietal delta as a candidate EEG marker.

papers.title: Integrative EEG/fMRI evidence for a multi-scale network underlying self-face and personal-object recognition.
papers.journal: Cortex; a journal devoted to the study of the nervous system and behavior
papers.summary: Using EEG and fMRI in 30 participants, the study found ownership-related visuo-midfrontal activity, frequency-specific theta inter-source phase coherence, and right hemisphere subnetworks (inferior temporal, middle frontal, inferior frontal, superior parietal). Results support a hybrid model where stimulus-specific visual pathways interact with domain-general frontal self-relevance encoding.

papers.title: Controlled deep breathing technique intervention effects on resting EEG, subjective psychological distress, and executive function performance in young adults.
papers.summary: A randomized controlled trial with 40 healthy adults found that a 20-minute controlled deep breathing intervention significantly increased resting-state EEG alpha/beta ratios (especially eyes-closed, parietal), reduced psychological distress, and improved executive function, compared to natural breathing controls.

papers.title: Electrophysiological signature of stroke recovery: investigating EEG biomarkers for prognostic insights.
papers.summary: In stroke patients, resting-state EEG at 1 week and 3 months post-stroke showed that change in relative alpha power was the strongest single correlate of motor improvement (ΔFM). A hierarchical model combining alpha power, metastability/synchrony, and microstates explained over 78% of variance in motor recovery, suggesting that balanced alpha oscillations and flexible network coordination index recovery.

papers.title: Multimodal art intervention for flourishing in lonely university students: psychological and exploratory neurophysiological outcomes.
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial with 60 lonely university students, an eight-week multimodal art intervention produced significant Group×Time improvements in psychological flourishing, positive affect, aesthetic experience, and an alpha-based relaxation EEG index, but not in attention-related EEG indices.

papers.title: Comprehensive Multimodal Diagnostics and Rehabilitation in Persistent Post-Concussion Syndrome Following Motor Vehicle Collision.
papers.summary: A case report of a 57-year-old woman with persistent post-concussion syndrome after a motor vehicle collision whose CT and brain MRI with SWI/DTI were unremarkable, while multimodal functional testing identified abnormalities across eight domains including vestibular, qEEG, pupillary autonomic, postural, oculomotor, cardiac autonomic, olfactory, and cognitive measures. A 10-modality rehabilitation program was followed by Concussion Symptom Checklist scores falling from 92 to 0 by 17 weeks post-injury.

papers.title: Neurite Complexity and Plasticity Markers Track Synaptic Vesicle Density in the Living Human Brain: A Multimodal PET-MRI-EEG Study
papers.summary: Combined [11C]-UCBJ PET, DWI/NODDI, rs-fMRI, and EEG in 18 healthy volunteers to test relationships between synaptic SV2A density and structural/functional plasticity markers, with ketamine (n=11) or DMT (n=7) challenge. BPND was coupled with neurite orientation dispersion across cortical regions and associated with EEG measures of short-term and long-term synaptic plasticity, while no consistent association was found with rs-fMRI functional weighted degree.

papers.title: EEG-Derived Pain Threshold Index-Guided Remifentanil Titration During Laparoscopic Abdominal Surgery: A Randomized Trial.
papers.summary: This randomized trial tested whether remifentanil titration guided by the EEG-derived pain threshold index reduces intraoperative remifentanil infusion during laparoscopic abdominal surgery. It found no significant difference in the primary endpoint: mean remifentanil infusion rate was 7.44 vs 7.63 µg kg-1 h-1 (adjusted difference -0.06; P=0.758). Exploratory secondary analyses showed lower PACU rescue opioid use and fewer PONV events with PTi guidance, but no reduction in total postoperative opioid exposure.

papers.title: Open-Loop Deep Brain Stimulation Versus Closed-Loop Responsive Neurostimulation in Drug-Resistant Bitemporal Epilepsy: A Narrative Review.
papers.journal: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology
papers.summary: This narrative review compared open-loop deep brain stimulation and closed-loop responsive neurostimulation for drug-resistant bitemporal epilepsy across 39 included studies, reporting median seizure reduction of approximately 60% to 75% with both modalities but limited seizure freedom. It concludes that RNS may be advantageous in focal or asymmetric bitemporal epilepsy and that treatment selection should be individualized.

papers.title: Dual-pathway processing of AI-generated Chinese ink painting: evidence from eye-tracking, EEG, and artistic expertise.
papers.summary: A multimodal eye-tracking, EEG, and rating study with 120 participants found that AI-generated Chinese ink paintings elicited higher scan-path entropy and beta band suppression than traditional or digital non-AI works, indicating greater attentional exploration; professional and non-professional viewers agreed on expressiveness but differed on cultural authenticity, supporting a dual-pathway framework.

papers.title: A comprehensive investigation into EEG spectral analysis for ADHD brain dominance.
papers.summary: EEG spectral analysis revealed atypical brain lateralization in ADHD: higher average power spectral density in the right brain during working states and left brain during resting states, with theta and alpha waves more dominant in left hemisphere across task states and theta prominent frontally.

papers.title: Sustained Seizure Freedom After Stereo-Electroencephalography Without Definitive Intervention: Evidence for Network Modulation by Invasive EEG.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
papers.summary: Reported two patients with drug-resistant epilepsy who achieved sustained seizure freedom after stereo-EEG monitoring without resection, ablation, or neuromodulation. The findings suggest that sEEG implantation may have microlesional or network-modulatory effects, and that extended follow-up may be warranted when habitual seizures are not captured and early improvement occurs.

papers.title: Stress recovery and restorative effects of viewing different types of peony garden landscapes: a preliminary experiment.
papers.summary: Preliminary VR experiment with 56 participants per group compared stress recovery after viewing flatland, terraced, or mountainous peony gardens versus an indoor environment using TSST, physiological measures (HR, HRV, EEG), and psychological scales. Peony garden scenes improved physiological and emotional recovery relative to the indoor scene, with the most pronounced changes after the mountainous peony garden.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
